```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The text fields take effect on "Draw samples"; the two selects are
// always-live. Each count is clamped so one run stays under a few seconds.
committed = {
  plotTrigger
  const read = (view, fallback, lo, hi) => {
    const v = VM.expressions.makeNumber(window.math, view.value)
    return Number.isFinite(v) ? Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, Math.round(v))) : fallback
  }
  const n = read(viewof nInput, 30, 2, 500)
  const R = read(viewof intervalsInput, 200, 1, 2000)
  const N = read(viewof resamplesInput, 1000, 50, 5000)
  const seed = read(viewof seedInput, 1, -1e9, 1e9)
  VM.ui.syncUrlParams({
    pop: [popSelect, defaults.pop], stat: [statSelect, defaults.stat],
    n: [(viewof nInput).value, defaults.n], intervals: [(viewof intervalsInput).value, defaults.intervals],
    resamples: [(viewof resamplesInput).value, defaults.resamples], seed: [(viewof seedInput).value, defaults.seed]
  })
  return {pop: popSelect, stat: statSelect, n, R, N, seed}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// result: every interval of the run, and the fixed x range they all fit in.
result = {
  const {pop, stat, n, R, N, seed} = committed
  const run = coverageRun({pop, stat, n, R, N, rng: VM.sampling.seededRandom(seed)})
  if (!Number.isFinite(run.truth)) return {ok: false, R, message: `${populationLabels.get(pop)} has no finite ${statLabels.get(stat).toLowerCase()} to cover.`}
  // The 1st and 99th percentiles of the endpoints, so one wild interval
  // (a skewed population's) doesn't squeeze all the others; it runs off
  // the edge instead.
  const los = run.intervals.map(iv => iv.lo).sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const his = run.intervals.map(iv => iv.hi).sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const lo = Math.min(run.truth, los[Math.floor(0.01 * (los.length - 1))])
  const hi = Math.max(run.truth, his[Math.ceil(0.99 * (his.length - 1))])
  const pad = (hi - lo) * 0.04 || 0.1
  return {ok: true, ...run, R, xRange: [lo - pad, hi + pad]}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
setup = {
  const k = Math.min(Number(stepControl), result.R)
  if (!result.ok) return {ok: false, k}
  const shown = result.intervals.slice(0, k)
  const hits = shown.filter(iv => iv.hit).length
  return {ok: true, k, shown, hits}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
mainPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  return (setup) => {
    const data = [], shapes = []
    const layout = {
      xaxis: {title: statLabels.get(committed.stat)},
      yaxis: {title: "sample", range: [0, result.R + 1], zeroline: false},
      hovermode: "closest", uirevision: "static", autosize: true, shapes
    }

    if (!setup.ok) {
      layout.annotations = VM.plotting.emptyState(result.message)
    } else {
      layout.xaxis.range = result.xRange
      // One trace for the hits and one for the misses, each interval a
      // segment, separated by nulls.
      const width = result.R > 400 ? 1 : result.R > 100 ? 2 : 4
      for (const [hit, color, name] of [[true, chartColors.ok, "covers"], [false, chartColors.alt, "misses"]]) {
        const xs = [], ys = []
        setup.shown.forEach((iv, i) => {
          if (iv.hit !== hit) return
          xs.push(iv.lo, iv.hi, null)
          ys.push(i + 1, i + 1, null)
        })
        data.push({x: xs, y: ys, type: "scatter", mode: "lines", name, showlegend: false, line: {color, width}, hoverinfo: "skip"})
      }
      data.push({
        x: setup.shown.map(iv => iv.estimate), y: setup.shown.map((_, i) => i + 1),
        customdata: setup.shown.map(iv => [iv.lo, iv.hi]),
        type: "scatter", mode: "markers", name: "estimate", showlegend: false,
        marker: {color: chartColors.ink, size: Math.max(2, width + 1)},
        hovertemplate: "sample %{y}<br>estimate %{x:.4g}<br>interval [%{customdata[0]:.4g}, %{customdata[1]:.4g}]<extra></extra>"
      })
      shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "paper", x0: result.truth, x1: result.truth, y0: 0, y1: 1, line: {color: chartColors.ink, width: 2, dash: "dash"}})
      layout.annotations = [{xref: "x", yref: "paper", x: result.truth, y: 1, yanchor: "bottom", showarrow: false, text: `true ${statLabels.get(committed.stat).toLowerCase()} = ${result.truth.toPrecision(4)}`, font: {color: chartColors.ink}}]
    }

    const config = VM.plotting.config()
    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
stats = {
  const items = [{label: "Intervals k", value: setup.k.toLocaleString()}]
  if (setup.ok) {
    items.push({label: "Cover the truth", value: setup.hits.toLocaleString()})
    items.push({label: "Coverage", value: setup.k ? `${(100 * setup.hits / setup.k).toFixed(1)}%` : "—", title: "Nominal coverage is 95%."})
  }
  return VM.ui.statRow(items)
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof stepControl = {
  const start = initialK === null ? result.R : Math.min(result.R, Math.max(0, Math.round(initialK)))
  const slider = Inputs.range([0, result.R], {step: 1, value: start, label: "k"})
  slider.classList.add("ojs-fill")
  return slider
}
```

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" title="Running coverage"}

```{ojs}
// Coverage of the first j intervals, against 95% and the band a correct
// 95% procedure would stay inside about 95% of the time.
runningCoveragePlot = {
  if (!result.ok) return document.createElement("div")
  const rows = []
  let hits = 0
  result.intervals.forEach((iv, i) => {
    if (iv.hit) hits++
    const j = i + 1
    const half = 1.96 * Math.sqrt(0.95 * 0.05 / j)
    rows.push({j, coverage: hits / j, lo: Math.max(0, 0.95 - half), hi: Math.min(1, 0.95 + half)})
  })
  return Plot.plot({
    height: 260, marginLeft: 46,
    x: {label: "intervals j"},
    y: {label: "coverage", domain: [0, 1], percent: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(rows, {x: "j", y1: "lo", y2: "hi", fill: chartColors.muted, fillOpacity: 0.2}),
      Plot.ruleY([0.95], {stroke: chartColors.muted, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
      Plot.lineY(rows, {x: "j", y: "coverage", stroke: chartColors.fn, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX([setup.k], {stroke: chartColors.warn})
    ]
  })
}
```
